events.title: The Siege of Jerusalem Begins
events.description: Crusader forces from the First Crusade reached Jerusalem and began a five-week siege of the city, which was held by the Fatimid Caliphate.
events.significance: The siege ended with the crusaders capturing Jerusalem in July 1099. That led to the founding of the Crusader states in the Levant.

events.title: The Treaty of Tordesillas Is Signed
events.description: Spain and Portugal agreed to divide newly encountered lands outside Europe between them along a north–south line in the Atlantic.
events.significance: The treaty shaped colonial claims in the Americas, Africa and Asia. It helps explain why Portuguese is spoken in Brazil and Spanish across most of Latin America.

events.title: Lee Proposes American Independence
events.description: Virginia delegate Richard Henry Lee presented a resolution to the Second Continental Congress. It declared that the Thirteen Colonies should be free and independent states.
events.significance: The resolution set in motion the drafting of the Declaration of Independence. Congress adopted that document a few weeks later.

events.title: Norway Dissolves Its Union with Sweden
events.description: The Norwegian parliament unanimously declared the union with Sweden to be dissolved after years of growing dissatisfaction.
events.significance: The declaration led to Norway's full independence as a sovereign monarchy. It was achieved peacefully.

events.title: Vatican City Becomes an Independent State
events.description: The Lateran Treaty had been signed in February of that year. On this day it was ratified, which created the sovereign state of Vatican City within Rome.
events.significance: The ratification settled decades of tension between the papacy and the Italian state. It established the Vatican as the world's smallest independent country.
